is_anopheles.evidence: The study investigates Anopheles gambiae sensu lato (s.l.) populations in Niger (Abstract, page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F (kdr-L1014F), Vgsc L995S (kdr-L1014S), and Ace-1 G280S (G119S) (Abstract, page 1; Methods, page 4).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 3 (page 10) provides detailed genotype counts (RR, RS, SS) for kdr-L1014F, kdr-L1014S, and Ace-1 G119S for dead and alive mosquitoes across 15 sites.

african_field_population.evidence: The study uses field-collected larvae and pupae from 16 sites in Niger (Methods, page 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting original insecticide resistance monitoring data from Niger.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study provides data for 15 specific districts/sites in Niger (e.g., Agadez, Balleyara, Boboye, etc.) (Table 3, page 10).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study reports data collected in 2019 and 2020 (Methods, page 3).

duplicate_risk.evidence: This is a countrywide monitoring study conducted by the NMCP and PMI VectorLink, representing new data for the specified years.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype data is provided in Table 3 of the main text.

assessment.summary: This study monitored insecticide resistance in Anopheles gambiae s.l. across 15 sites in Niger during 2019 and 2020. It assessed susceptibility to pyrethroids and chlorfenapyr, and characterized resistance markers (kdr-L1014F, kdr-L1014S, and Ace-1 G119S). The study reports high pyrethroid resistance and the first detection of the L1014S mutation in Niger.
